curriculum.lesson_evidence: Dancers can move alone, with a partner or in a group. Mirroring is when a partner copies your movement as if they are your reflection. Unison is when everyone does the same movement at the same time. Contrast is when partners do different movements, such as one high and one low. Partners need to look at each other, move at the same speed and keep a safe distance. Never push or pull your partner, and use only gentle contact if you agree. If you do not want to dance with someone, you may dance alongside them instead.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Plan a four-count partner phrase using mirroring for the first two counts and contrast for the last two. Say what each partner does.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Counts 1 and 2: both sweep their arms out, mirrored. Counts 3 and 4: one drops low and the other stretches high.' Mirroring shows togetherness and contrast shows difference.

WATCH FOR
Believing that dancing with a partner means holding hands or touching. Many partner and group dances have no contact and still show connection through eye contact, timing and shape.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a partner or group phrase with mirroring, unison and contrast. Write the plan with counts, rehearse with a family member and note how you kept in time. Swap roles.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

WORKED MODEL
